_note: Vassals (war-and-realm §4; docs/diplomacy-design.md §9). Fealty, not absorption: a vassal keeps its own faction, family, lands, armies and banners. PLACEHOLDER numbers.
_cap_note: No vassal may exceed cap_share of its overlord's total strength (regions x 10 plus army power; core/reputation.gd strength). The vassal AI stops expanding at the cap.

gains._note: Loyalty rises (war-and-realm §4.4) with marriages, protection, shared enemies, gifts (per gift_gold), honouring oaths, winning wars together, helping their goals, time (up to time_to), titles granted.

losses._note: Loyalty only falls through neglect (goals ignored: neglect per turn after neglect_after turns; calls for help ignored), dishonour (betrayal, attacking a fellow vassal), humiliation (banners called with no plunder or glory) and enemy intrigue (hook). Every change is logged with its reason.

_warn_note: A neglected vassal at rock bottom shows multi-turn warnings (warning_turns countdown); the breakaway itself is deferred to the realm-mechanics part (hook only).
_reliable_note: Obligations (war calls, troops, tribute) are always met at loyalty reliable_at or more; below it each is a chance of loyalty / reliable_at (diplomacy-design §18.11).

econ_goals._note: Broad economic goals the overlord sets per vassal (war-and-realm §4.2); the vassal AI's construction weights by category.

goals._note: Personal goals (war-and-realm §4.3): land (a neighbouring region they want), marriage (into your family), title (one of your lesser titles), revenge (war on a rival). Helping (the goal met) earns goal_helped loyalty and gives the overlord a cut: cut_gold gold, or the troops and land shares the AI handles.
